subject: Urgent: sudden request denials impacting batch inference (429/504)
messages:
From: Anna Diaz <anna.diaz@medsync.health>
To: markus.klein@redwoodai.com
Cc: platform@medsync.health
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: sudden surge - bulk job failing with 429/504

Hi Markus,

We're seeing a sustained spike in request denials from Redwood for our nightly batch jobs starting ~07:55 PST. Around 40% of calls return 429, a smaller but non-trivial portion are timing out with 504. This wasn't happening yesterday. It's impacting our overnight inference run and slowing downstream reporting.

I've attached a small log snippet (medsync_429_log_snip.txt) with sample request IDs and timestamps. Our team also noticed spikes in retries which make the window worse. Can you confirm whether any quota/tiering changes were made on your side or if this looks like a misapplied org/project cap?

We need immediate mitigation — even a short-term increase to concurrency or temporary bypass so our batch can finish.

Thanks,
Anna Diaz
Head of Core Platform
MedSync Health

From: markus.klein@redwoodai.com
To: Anna Diaz <anna.diaz@medsync.health>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwoodai.com, laura_bennett@redwoodai.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: sudden surge - bulk job failing with 429/504

Anna — thanks for the heads up and for the log snippet. I'm taking point on this.

Quick update: I don't see any scheduled config changes for MedSync in our rollout calendar, but I want engineering to confirm whether the org-level limits or a tier assignment flip triggered the behavior. Rishi, can you triage the tenant (medsync-org-7832) and confirm whether quota mapping or a recent routing policy changed?

Laura — please loop in CS playbook for temporary credits / burst overrides if we need to raise capacity immediately. Jordan, FYI in case execs ask.

We can also consider diverting this customer's batch to an alternate compatible instance while we investigate. Will update in 30–45 minutes.

— Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Customer Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwoodai.com
To: markus.klein@redwoodai.com, Anna Diaz <anna.diaz@medsync.health>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodai.com, grace_oconnor@redwoodai.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: sudden surge - bulk job failing with 429/504

Markus / Anna — quick triage notes from infra:

- Observed: starting 07:50 PST we see a sudden rise in 429 errors for medsync-org-7832 originating from the project-level router. Token bucket exhaustion correlated with a large batch job that increased request concurrency beyond the project limit.
- Cause hypothesis: a recent housekeeping change in our tiering service (deploy 2026-11-24 03:10 UTC) adjusted several orgs' default project caps while backfilling metadata; one project mapping for MedSync was incorrectly set to the lower 'starter' cap instead of 'scale' cap due to a metadata key mismatch.
- Immediate mitigation performed: bumped project cap for medsync-org-7832 to previous scale value, enabled emergency burst allowance for 30 minutes, and applied a short-lived routing exception to route batch traffic to dedicated pool D-Pool-07.

Anna — you should see a reduction in 429s now; please confirm. Also attaching a sample request id matrix and log snippet for reference.

Follow-up items I'm creating: JIRA-OPS-9142 (investigate tiering deploy failure + add canary), and we'll roll out a hotfix to avoid metadata backfill collisions.

-rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Anna Diaz <anna.diaz@medsync.health>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwoodai.com, markus.klein@redwoodai.com
Cc: platform@medsync.health
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: sudden surge - bulk job failing with 429/504

Thanks Rishi — we see an immediate drop in 429s for the in-flight window. Batch resumed and most jobs are finishing. We'll continue to monitor the rest of today's runs.

Two asks while you fix the root cause:
1) Can you share an ETA for the hotfix and the rollout plan?
2) We need an updated mutual action plan that includes an SLA exception or temporary capacity guarantee in case this happens during a critical window. I'm attaching MAP v2 for your ops/CS to review.

Appreciate the quick response.

Anna
From: laura_bennett@redwoodai.com
To: Anna Diaz <anna.diaz@medsync.health>
Cc: markus.klein@redwoodai.com, rishi_malhotra@redwoodai.com, grace_oconnor@redwoodai.com, jordan_blake@redwoodai.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: sudden surge - bulk job failing with 429/504

Anna — thanks for confirming. We've received the MAP v2 and started an internal review. Proposed next steps: 

- Immediate: issue a one-time operational credit for the affected window (pending approvals) and create a short-term SLA addendum to cover emergency capacity for nightly batch jobs while the hotfix is deployed.
- Near term (48–72h): Rishi's team to validate hotfix on canary, then staged rollout. We'll provide a rollout timeline by EOD tomorrow.
- Long term: add more conservative live checks to the tiering backfill job (pre/post sanity) and enforce a canary policy for metadata backfills.

I'll open a HubSpot note on the deal and attach the timeline + credit estimate. Jordan — flag this for leadership awareness; execs may request an RCA and credit ask.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
From: jordan_blake@redwoodai.com
To: markus.klein@redwoodai.com, laura_bennett@redwoodai.com, rishi_malhotra@redwoodai.com, Anna Diaz <anna.diaz@medsync.health>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 17:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: sudden surge - bulk job failing with 429/504

Team — quick leadership note for the record before tomorrow's exec sync: 

- Status: customer batch throughput recovered; temporary burst and routing exception removed at 15:30 PST on 2026-11-24. No further 429 spikes observed in the last 36 hours.
- RCA (high level): metadata backfill during tiering deployment matched a legacy key for one of MedSync's projects and dropped it to starter-level caps. This was not caught by the current canary because the metadata backfill path was not exercised in canary.
- Impact: one overnight run partially failed; customer operational impact minimal but real — they requested credits and an SLA exception.
- Action items: JIRA-OPS-9142 (Rishi) — fix backfill + add canary; OPS to publish postmortem and credit estimate (Laura); Engineering to add a short-runpoint to the rollout checklist to avoid project cap regressions; CS to update MAP.

I'll be ready to brief execs with the postmortem draft tomorrow morning. Mark, Rishi — please send me the postmortem link and credit estimate by 09:00 PST.

-jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
